plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked pH and ulcer-cause chart shows William Beaumont's 1825–1833 gastric fistula experiments (pH 1.5–2.0 hydrochloric acid dissolving meat in 2–4 hours) alongside Robin Warren and Barry Marshall's 1982–1984 discovery of Helicobacter pylori using urease enzyme to neutralise stomach acid in an ammonia shield and cause ~80% of gastric ulcers and ~90% of duodenal ulcers.

teach_overlay.label: PH 1.5 GASTRIC ACID VS H. PYLORI UREASE AMMONIA SHIELD (80–90% OF ULCERS)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked pH and ulcer-cause chart on period paper showing human stomach acid at pH 1.5–2.0 (nearly as acidic as battery acid at pH 0.8 and 10⁶× more acidic than pure water at pH 7.0) and H. pylori causing ~80% of gastric ulcers and ~90% of duodenal ulcers
teach_overlay.scale: human stomach acid sits near pH 1.5 — strong enough to dissolve a zinc nail and a million times more acidic than pure water, yet H. pylori wraps itself in an ammonia bubble to survive inside it
